title: From Adam to Israel's Neighbors
overview: The writer opens his history of Israel with a family tree running from the first human through Noah's sons and Abraham, briefly listing related nations before narrowing toward Israel.

parts.label: Adam to Noah (vv. 1-4)
parts.note: These bare names, taken from Genesis, trace ten generations from the first human to Noah, who survived the flood, and then his three sons. Most scholars think Chronicles was written after the Jewish people returned from exile in Babylon, and starting with Adam places their small community inside the story of all humanity.

parts.label: The nations from Noah's sons (vv. 5-23)
parts.note: Copied in shortened form from Genesis 10, this list links known peoples to Noah's sons: Japheth to peoples north and west such as the Greeks (Javan), Ham to Egypt, Cush and Canaan, and Shem to peoples east such as Assyria and Aram. Many names are really peoples or places rather than single persons, and scholars are unsure what the note about the earth being 'divided' in Peleg's day refers to.

parts.label: Shem's line to Abraham (vv. 24-27)
parts.note: The list now drops every other branch and follows a single line of ten names from Shem down to Abraham, the ancestor of Israel. Christians later read this line as part of Jesus' ancestry, since Luke's Gospel traces him back through these same names to Adam.

parts.label: Abraham's other sons (vv. 28-33)
parts.note: Ishmael's twelve sons became tribes of the Arabian desert, and the sons of Keturah, a concubine (a wife of lower status), included Midian, a people Israel often met later. They are named and then set aside as the story moves to Isaac's family.

parts.label: Esau and the land of Edom (vv. 34-54)
parts.note: Esau, Jacob's twin brother, was the ancestor of Edom, Israel's close neighbor and frequent rival, and the list also includes Seir's sons, who were earlier inhabitants of that region. The kings and chiefs, taken from Genesis 36, show Edom had rulers before Israel did, and each king seems to come from a different town rather than passing the throne from father to son.

disagreement: Christians differ on whether lists like this are complete family records that can be used to date human history, or selective, shaped lists meant to show relationships between peoples rather than every generation.
think: What do you think is gained, or lost, when a people tells its story by starting with the whole human race rather than with itself?
